Here’s a quick‑look list of the Canadian public holidays that give you a **three‑day long weekend** in 2023.  
(If a holiday falls on a weekend, the “observed” day is usually the following Monday, which still creates a long weekend.)

| Holiday | Date in 2023 | How it creates a long weekend |
|---------|--------------|--------------------------------|
| **New Year’s Day** | Jan 1 (Observed Mon Jan 2) | Weekend: Sat Dec 31 – Mon Jan 2 |
| **Good Friday** | Apr 7 | Weekend: Fri Apr 7 – Sun Apr 9 |
| **Victoria Day** | May 22 (Mon) | Weekend: Sat May 20 – Mon May 22 |
| **Canada Day** | Jul 1 (Sat) (Observed Mon Jul 3) | Weekend: Sat Jul 1 – Mon Jul 3 |
| **Labour Day** | Sep 4 (Mon) | Weekend: Sat Sep 2 – Mon Sep 4 |
| **Thanksgiving** | Oct 9 (Mon) | Weekend: Sat Oct 7 – Mon Oct 9 |
| **Remembrance Day** | Nov 11 (Fri) | Weekend: Fri Nov 11 – Sun Nov 13 |
| **Christmas Day** | Dec 25 (Mon) | Weekend: Sat Dec 23 – Mon Dec 25 |

> **Note:** Boxing Day (Dec 26 Tue) does not create a long weekend in 2023, as it falls on a Tuesday.

These are the federal holidays that give you a natural break. Provincial holidays (e.g., Family Day, St. Patrick’s Day, etc.) can also create long weekends in specific provinces, but the above list covers the nationwide long‑weekend opportunities for 2023.
